note: Project summaries distinguish documented contributions, research objectives and related publications. Statuses and dates remain in project-statuses.json. Illustrations are schematics, not experimental evidence. Outputs are sourced individually, with explicit lab, consortium and related-work attribution. Unverified project-specific results are not inferred.

projects.name: WalleSmart
projects.image_alt: Connected field, satellite and weather data flowing into the WalleSmart cloud platform.
projects.summary: An interoperable cloud platform connecting farm sensors, satellite imagery and weather data to agricultural decision tools in Wallonia.
projects.focus: Scalable data processing and integration of heterogeneous agricultural data, developed and evaluated with real farms and weather stations.
projects.relationship_note: The cited paper explicitly presents and evaluates the WALLeSmart platform.

outputs.title: Cloud architecture tested with agricultural data
outputs.description: Roukh and Mahmoudi evaluated WALLeSmart with data from 30 dairy farms and 32 weather stations in Wallonia. The published architecture combines real-time and batch processing, a modular plugin system and agricultural data exchange.
outputs.verification: The paper explicitly presents WALLeSmart; the field sample is stated in its introduction. These are study data sources, not a count of current platform customers.

outputs.title: Applications farmers can use
outputs.description: The platform provides a shared sign-in, a personalised dashboard, data-sharing consent controls and access to agricultural applications. CRA-W confirms that W@llHerbe is available through WALLeSmart for daily grass-biomass estimates.
outputs.verification: Both service availability and the W@llHerbe application are documented by their operators. W@llHerbe is attributed to CRA-W, not presented as software authored solely by SMART’ILIA.

projects.name: AI4BRAIN
projects.image_alt: MRI and clinical data combined through multimodal learning.
projects.summary: AI methods for psychiatric and neurodegenerative disease research, developed with clinical and neuroscience partners.
projects.focus: Brain MRI segmentation and AI architectures for detecting and classifying neurodegenerative diseases, with Saïd Mahmoudi contributing to model development.
projects.relationship_note: MPB-UNet is listed on the official AI4Brain publications page. The newer multimodal study is related lab research; its funding is not attributed here.

outputs.title: MPB-UNet brain MRI segmentation
outputs.description: Chahbar, Merati and Mahmoudi published a multi-parallel UNet method evaluated on the LGG MRI dataset. Table 5 reports an average Dice score of 94.43% and IoU of 92.17% on the test set; these are dataset results, not clinical validation.
outputs.verification: The official AI4Brain publications page lists MPB-UNet. Metrics are from Table 5, page 14, not the different aggregate scores in the abstract. DOI volume is 2025; original publication date is 26 December 2024.

projects.name: ARIAC
projects.summary: Trustworthy AI research within the TRAIL initiative, supporting the deployment of reliable models in real-world settings.
projects.focus: Efficient AI implementation: edge deployment, distributed learning and high-performance computing, within TRAIL’s implementation work package.
projects.relationship_note: TRAIL records Sidi Ahmed Mahmoudi’s participation in ARIAC WP4; no unverified project result or performance figure is asserted.

outputs.title: AI-based scheduling across CPU and GPU nodes
outputs.description: A study co-authored by Sidi Mahmoudi implements continuous monitoring and AI-based load estimates to schedule tasks across heterogeneous nodes. It evaluates execution time, throughput, resource use and energy consumption against other scheduling methods.
outputs.verification: The paper substantiates implementation and evaluation. No ARIAC funding acknowledgement was found in the full text; it is explicitly labelled related lab research, not an ARIAC deliverable.

projects.name: TSV — Track Sentry Vision
projects.summary: Computer vision from on-train video for detecting railway track defects and supporting preventive maintenance.
projects.focus: Automated visual inspection of railway infrastructure. The linked 2025 study documents track-defect detection within the project.
projects.relationship_note: The official BNAIC/BeNeLearn 2025 poster paper acknowledges Track Sentry Vision funding. Its authors are not presented as SMART’ILIA members; the public project timeline remains unconfirmed.

outputs.title: Sensor-equipped railway inspection prototype
outputs.description: Crespin, Kostis and Schaus built a laboratory LEGO train with a Raspberry Pi 5, camera and accelerometer. Their TSV study reports a YOLOv11n F1 score of 0.96 for artificial obstacles; validation on operational railway tracks remains future work.
outputs.verification: The official conference paper names ICTEAM/INGI, UCLouvain, describes the prototype and gives the 0.96 laboratory F1 score. It is not presented as a SMART’ILIA-only implementation or a field-validated system.

projects.name: SiTies — Secure IoT for Smart Cities
projects.image_alt: A city grid with connected buildings, sensor nodes and secure IoT infrastructure.
projects.summary: An international NATO Science for Peace and Security collaboration on secure IoT infrastructure for connected cities.
projects.focus: Secure connectivity, cyberthreat detection and network infrastructure for distributed urban sensors.
projects.relationship_note: The registry establishes project scope and dates; the institutional InCyber brochure documents UMONS participation and research themes, rather than measured project outcomes.

outputs.title: CyberLab / CyberRange at UMONS
outputs.description: The institutional InCyber brochure documents the team’s CyberLab, connecting IT infrastructure with physical IoT sensors and actuators. This platform supports research on the interaction between cybersecurity and AI.
outputs.verification: The UMONS section, brochure printed page 15, explicitly says the team has set up CyberLab. It is related infrastructure described alongside SiTies; no SiTies-specific delivery or performance claim is inferred.

projects.name: ROAD-STEP
projects.summary: Remote monitoring and decision support for pasture-based livestock farming in Wallonia.
projects.focus: Electronic identification and animal data streams to support monitoring of cattle behaviour, health and welfare.
projects.relationship_note: The Kappa architecture paper is related lab research. CTA Strée’s ongoing listing is explicitly attributed; no final end date or project-specific performance is inferred.

outputs.title: W@llHerbe grassland decision support
outputs.description: W@llHerbe combines satellite imagery and a growth model to estimate daily grass biomass per parcel. CRA-W identifies ROAD-STEP among the development collaborations and confirms the first version is available on WALLeSmart.
outputs.verification: The 2023 CRA-W article establishes the ROAD-STEP/SUNSHINE/WALLeSmart collaboration; the 30 July 2026 article confirms actual availability and attributes tool development to CRA-W.

projects.name: FEDER-IDEES

projects.name: IMOTION (Chist-Era)
projects.summary: Multimodal video retrieval using images, movement information and interactive queries such as sketches and speech.

outputs.title: Multimodal retrieval and open-source software
outputs.description: The consortium report documents an integrated system supporting sketch, image, motion and speech queries. UMONS contributed deep-learning features and sketch recognition. It also records the open-source vitrivr backend; the software project is maintained by the University of Basel.
outputs.verification: The official CHIST-ERA 2018 report describes UMONS work on slides 7 and 10, query modes on slide 11 and the open-source backend on slide 13. Current vitrivr documentation identifies the University of Basel as maintainer; consortium attribution is preserved.
